interface.title: SAEDscope
interface.field: Materials science / transmission electron microscopy (selected-area electron diffraction)
interface.stage_of_work: Analysis and interpretation of acquired diffraction patterns, plus planning the next acquisition (specimen tilt)
interface.what_it_is_for: Classify an electron diffraction pattern as single crystal, polycrystalline or amorphous, index its spots or rings against candidate phases, and report the best phase and zone axis with evidence, calibration flags and a suggested next tilt.

data.note: Source defaults to 'Upload a file'. All work switched it to 'Try an example' and used the built-in simulated examples: gold rings, NiAl rings, Si [011], amorphous metallic glass, and the hexagonal look-alike pattern. Each example shows its true answer. No test files were available (browser_list_files returned none), so uploads, CIF checks and batch mode could not be run. Only the built-in explainer was used; no Anthropic, OpenAI or Materials Project keys were entered.

features.name: Tilt planner with predicted post-tilt patterns
features.general: List candidate follow-up measurements; select one to see side by side what the current data looks like and what each competing hypothesis predicts you would see after it, with a table of hypothesis scores
features.specific: In the Next step tab, pick a 'Tilt N°: phase → [uvw]' radio; the panel shows the measured spots with the dashed tilt axis next to the simulated pattern for each candidate phase/zone after the tilt, plus text giving the expected spot d-spacings and angles, and a candidate/zone/score/orientation-fit table
steps: Run the analysis on a spot pattern
Open the Next step tab
Select one of the suggested tilts
Compare the 'Now (measured)' panel with each candidate's predicted panel
Read the expected d-spacings and angles to check at the microscope
serves_tasks: Choose a specimen tilt that confirms an answer or tells competing answers apart

features.name: Indexed pattern overlay linked with a simulated reference
features.general: Show the measured image with each detected feature labelled by its best-fit assignment, beside an idealised simulation marking predicted features as observed or not; hover a feature for its values, zoom and pan the image
features.specific: Plotly image of the SAED pattern with spots circled and hkl-labelled, g1/g2 basis vectors and centre cross, next to 'Simulated [uvw] zone of phase' (filled = predicted and observed, open = predicted, not observed); hover shows '(hkl): d = x Å (ref y)'; wheel zooms
steps: Analyse a spot pattern
Hover a circled spot to read its hkl and d
Scroll on the image to zoom
Compare against the simulated zone panel
serves_tasks: Find the phase and viewing direction that explain a spot pattern

features.name: Radial profile with reference line markers
features.general: Average a 2-D ring pattern into a 1-D intensity profile against reciprocal spacing, fit a background, and draw reference lines from the best candidate so peaks and expected positions can be compared
features.specific: Log-intensity radial profile vs g = 1/d (Å⁻¹) with dashed background and phase reference sticks, paired with the ring overlay on the image; the same plot is used for amorphous halos (dashed halo markers)
steps: Analyse a ring or halo pattern
Read peak positions against the reference sticks
Check the overlay rings on the image
Change the calibration and re-run to see the sticks shift
serves_tasks: Identify the phase producing a ring pattern
Check for rings the best phase leaves unexplained
Estimate the typical atomic spacing from a diffuse halo

features.name: Calibration method selector with consistency flags
features.general: Choose how raw pixel distances become physical units from several methods, each with its own inputs; after fitting, flag how far the data deviate from the reference so a bad calibration is visible
features.specific: 'How is the pattern calibrated?' dropdown (file, standard pattern + material, scale bar value/unit/length, nm⁻¹/px, Å⁻¹/px, voltage + camera length + pixel size, ratios only); verdict chips such as 'Calibrated (user)', 'd-spacings offset -5.7% from reference', 'Calibrated (camera length)' and 'Uncalibrated: ratios only'
steps: Open the calibration dropdown
Pick a method
Fill in its fields (e.g. Å⁻¹ per pixel)
Analyse pattern
Read the offset or uncalibrated chip and the explanation
serves_tasks: Find out by how much a nominal calibration is off
